t: A Late Bronze Age port-kingdom at Ras Shamra on the Syrian coast, trading with Egypt, Cyprus, the Aegean and Mesopotamia.
Its scribes used a 30-sign cuneiform alphabet and recorded the Baal cycle and the epics of Kirta and Aqhat.
A vassal of Egypt and then the Hittites, it was destroyed by seaborne raiders c. 1185 BCE and never rebuilt.
dyk: Many of Ugarit’s clay tablets survived because the fire that destroyed the city baked them hard; some of its last letters report enemy ships off the coast.
ev: King Zimri-Lim of Mari visits Ugarit
Niqmaddu II becomes a vassal of the Hittite king Suppiluliuma I
Ugaritic troops fight for the Hittites at the Battle of Kadesh
Ugarit reaches the height of its prosperity under Ammishtamru II
The city is sacked and burned, probably by seaborne raiders
A farmer’s discovery of a tomb at Minet el-Beida leads to excavations
Claude Schaeffer begins excavating Ras Shamra
